prompt: Why are traces the signal that usually gets sampled, rather than metrics?
hint: What does each one grow with?

choices.text: Traces are less useful than metrics during an incident
choices.why: They answer a different question, not a lesser one.

choices.text: A trace grows with every request; a metric grows with its labels
Metrics cannot be sampled at all
choices.why: The reason is cost, not possibility.

choices.text: Trace stores refuse more than a fixed number of spans
choices.why: No such limit was the reason.

prompt: The lab measured 4.5 checkouts and 35 spans a second. About how many spans does one checkout produce? Answer to the nearest whole number.
What is the main trade between deciding at the head and at the tail?
hint: When each decides, and what it knows then.

choices.text: The head is cheap and blind; the tail sees outcomes and holds every span
The head keeps errors; the tail keeps a fixed fraction
choices.why: It is the other way round.

choices.text: The head needs a Collector to decide; the tail needs only each service's SDK
They differ only in the fraction they keep
choices.why: They differ in what they can know.

prompt: A `traceparent` ends in `-02`. What does the receiving service with a parent-based sampler do?

choices.text: It records the trace, since `02` is above zero
choices.why: The low bit is what counts.

choices.text: It does not record it: the sampled bit is off
It makes its own decision with a fresh random number
choices.why: A parent-based sampler follows the parent.

choices.text: It rejects the request as malformed

prompt: How does `TraceIdRatioBased` decide whether to keep a trace?
hint: Two services reach the same answer without talking.

choices.text: It draws a fresh random number for every new span that any service starts
It keeps every tenth trace in the order they start
It reads the trace id as a number and keeps it below a bound
It asks the Collector how many traces it has stored

prompt: The sampler `parentbased_traceidratio` follows a parent if there is one, and otherwise keeps a fixed ___ of root traces.
Under head sampling at one in ten, a log line's trace id leads to "trace not found". What is the likeliest reason?

choices.text: The log line was written by a service with no SDK installed at all, so no trace exists
choices.why: It has an id, so it has an SDK.

choices.text: The trace was not sampled, though the line still carries its id
Jaeger has crashed and lost every trace it held
The id in the log is the span id, not the trace id
choices.why: The field is the trace id.

prompt: What is head sampling's main weakness?

choices.text: It costs more than tail sampling
It needs every service to be restarted daily so that the fraction applies
It drops slow and failed requests as readily as fast ones
It cannot be configured without changing code

prompt: The storefront samples one in ten, and `orders` is set to `always_on`. What appears in the store?

choices.text: Exactly the same traces as before the change
choices.why: orders now records the dropped ones too.

choices.text: Traces that start at orders, with a parent that was never exported
An error from the SDK refusing the setting
Nothing from orders at all

prompt: What rule keeps head-sampled traces whole?

choices.text: Every service samples its own fraction independently
Sample at the root; parent-based samplers everywhere else
Keep `always_on` in every service that is downstream of the root
choices.why: That records the dropped traces' middles.

choices.text: Sample only in the Collector
choices.why: That is tail sampling, a different scheme.

prompt: Upstream keeps 50% and downstream keeps 10%, both with plain `TraceIdRatioBased` on the same trace id. What happens to the traces between 10% and 50%?

choices.text: Both keep them, since the ids are the same
Neither keeps them
Upstream keeps them and downstream drops its part
Downstream keeps them and upstream drops its part

prompt: Why does the lab's tail sampler keep 5% of ordinary traces as well as errors and slow ones?

choices.text: To have a baseline of normal traces to compare problems with
Because the processor requires at least three policies before it will start
To keep span metrics accurate
choices.why: Those count every span before sampling.

choices.text: Because 5% of traces are always errors

prompt: Which of these can a tail sampling policy decide on? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: An error status on any span
The trace's total duration
An attribute's value, such as a customer id
Whether the customer will come back tomorrow
choices.why: Nothing in the trace knows that.

prompt: What does `decision_wait` set?

choices.text: How long a kept trace stays in Jaeger
How long after a trace's first span the Collector decides
How long a service waits before exporting a span
choices.why: That is the batch processor in the SDK.

choices.text: The latency above which a trace counts as slow
choices.why: That is the latency policy's threshold.

prompt: Put what happens to one trace under tail sampling in order.
hint: From the first span to the store.
items: Every service records and exports its spans
The Collector holds them under the trace id
The policies are evaluated on the whole trace
The trace is sent to the stores or dropped

prompt: Two Collectors sit behind an ordinary round-robin load balancer, both tail sampling. What goes wrong?
hint: Where the spans of one trace go.

choices.text: Nothing, since each Collector makes the same decision from the same trace id
Each sees part of a trace and judges it without the rest
The load balancer drops every span that carries an error status before it arrives
The two Collectors keep each trace twice

prompt: What is the `loadbalancing` exporter for, in front of tail samplers?

choices.text: It spreads spans evenly to cut each Collector's memory
It samples traces before they reach the second layer
choices.why: It routes; it does not sample.

choices.text: It sends all spans of a trace to the same Collector
It retries spans that a Collector refused
choices.why: That is not its purpose here.

prompt: During an outage the mailer takes messages 26 s late, and `decision_wait` is 10 s. What can happen to a kept checkout?
hint: The mailer's span arrives after the decision.

choices.text: Its decision is delayed until the mailer's span arrives
It ends up stored without the mailer's spans
choices.why: Right, once the decision is forgotten.

choices.text: The Collector refuses the mailer's span and logs an error
The mailer's span may be kept twice

prompt: Why must span metrics be computed before the sampler?

choices.text: The sampler deletes the attributes they need
After it, the spans left are a biased sample, not the traffic
Prometheus refuses metrics that come from a pipeline with a sampler in it
The connector cannot run after any processor in the same Collector's pipeline
choices.why: It can; the point is what it sees.

prompt: Under the lab's tail sampling, an error ratio is computed from the traces in Jaeger. How does it compare with the truth?
hint: Every error is kept, and 5% of the rest.

choices.text: It is exact, because every error is kept
It is about one tenth of the truth
It is several times too high
It cannot be computed at all

prompt: A span is named `GET /orders/1047` instead of `GET /orders/{id}`. What does the `spanmetrics` connector make of it?

choices.text: One series for all orders, as the connector strips numbers
A new series for every order
Nothing, as the connector skips server spans
An error for an invalid span name
choices.why: The name is valid, just costly.

prompt: An exemplar on `orders`' histogram opens to "trace not found" under tail sampling. Why?
hint: Who chose the exemplar, and when?

choices.text: The histogram chose it before the sampler dropped the trace
Prometheus corrupts trace ids it stores
Exemplars name spans, not traces
The trace was kept but not yet indexed

prompt: Under head sampling, how can exemplars be made to point only at kept traces?
hint: The decision is known during the request.

choices.text: Raise the sampling fraction to one half, so most exemplars find their trace
Attach an exemplar only when the span is sampled
Store exemplars in Jaeger instead of Prometheus
choices.why: That changes nothing about which trace exists.

choices.text: Drop the `#` part from the OpenMetrics output

prompt: A team head-samples 1% and complains that failed checkouts are never in Jaeger. What is the best change?
hint: Who can know a request failed?

choices.text: Raise the head fraction to 50%
choices.why: Half the failures still vanish, at fifty times the cost.

choices.text: Set `always_on` in the service that fails
Record everything and tail-sample, keeping every error
Count failures from the traces instead of from the logs, which are sampled too

prompt: Match each question to the signal that should answer it under sampling.
hint: Counts from metrics, stories from traces.

pairs.left: How many checkouts failed in the last hour?
pairs.right: span metrics or the service's own counters

pairs.left: Why did this one checkout fail?
What did each service say about it?
pairs.right: its log lines, by trace id

pairs.left: What does a normal checkout look like?

hint: Head sampling drops at the source.
